h1: IKKYU2 Ang Thong — a Small, Quiet Japanese-Style Boutique Stay
intro: If you want a place to stay in Ang Thong that's quiet, clean and has the feel of a small Japanese guesthouse — IKKYU2 Angthong is a name real reviews keep describing as "good value" and "clean". It's a small boutique stay in Mueang Ang Thong district, Phosa subdistrict, on the bypass road. Rooms come with air-con, a private balcony, Netflix on the TV and free parking, and the staff speak Thai, English and Japanese. Rates start at about ฿650/night. The trade-off is that, being a small place, there's no breakfast and you'll hear the odd footstep along the corridor.

body.html: What sets IKKYU2 apart from the usual places to stay in Ang Thong is that it's a small, carefully looked-after stay. It's a boutique property with only a handful of rooms, set up so each one feels clean and private rather than one of hundreds in a big block. The name IKKYU is Japanese, and the owner has woven in the feel of a small Japanese guesthouse. Several real reviews agree that the rooms are clean and tidy, and good value for what you pay.

Rooms are Standard King. Each comes with cool air-con, a TV with Netflix, a private balcony, an en-suite bathroom, a hair dryer and a work desk. The room size is comfortable for an overnight stay or a longer stretch of several days. Some reviews note the rooms are roomier than expected and well equipped. A favourite detail is being able to watch Netflix in bed — not something you find easily at this price in Ang Thong.

Another thing reviews praise often is the quiet and the friendly staff. The stay is on the bypass road, and the rooms are fairly quiet, which suits anyone who actually wants to rest. Staff get good marks for being helpful and for speaking several languages — Thai, English and Japanese. There's free on-site parking, so self-drivers park easily. The location is in Mueang Ang Thong, a few minutes' drive from the town's restaurant streets and markets.
"Very clean and tidy room, good value for what you get, lovely staff, and you can even watch Netflix in the room — nice and quiet for a stay in Ang Thong."

To be straight with you, the thing reviews flag most often on the downside is footstep noise along the corridor. Because it's a small building, you sometimes hear footsteps passing your door or from the floor above. If you're a light sleeper, the simplest fix is to bring earplugs or ask for a room that isn't on the main corridor when you book.

The other thing to know before booking is that there's no breakfast, and the convenience store and supermarket are too far to walk. You'll need to drive or ride out to find food. On top of that, the laundry is coin-operated, so if you want to wash clothes you'll need a handful of 10-baht coins. These come with the territory at a small place that focuses on the room itself rather than extra services, but they're worth planning around.

Overall, IKKYU2 scores around 9.0 out of 10 from real reviews on both Trip.com and Booking.com, which is high for Ang Thong. It's a sensible pick for anyone who wants a clean, quiet, private room at a low price and isn't fussed about breakfast. Prices start around ฿650 and rise with the season to roughly ฿800–900 when it's busy. If you can live with the corridor noise and the lack of breakfast, this place offers solid value for the price.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — IKKYU2 Ang Thong

faq.q: Where is IKKYU2 in Ang Thong, and what's nearby?
faq.a: IKKYU2 is at 71/47 Bypass Road, Phosa, Mueang Ang Thong. It's in town, a few minutes' drive from the markets and restaurant streets. Wat Khun Inthapramun is about 20 minutes away by car and Wat Muang about 25 minutes.

faq.q: How much does IKKYU2 cost, and what are the rooms like?
faq.a: Rates start at about ฿650/night for a Standard King room. Each room has air-con, a TV with Netflix, a private balcony and an en-suite bathroom. Prices rise with the season to roughly ฿800–900 when it's busy — always compare a few platforms before booking.
No — there's no breakfast service, and the convenience store and supermarket are too far to walk. It's best to drive or ride out to eat in town, or pick up some food to keep in the room.

faq.q: Does IKKYU2 have parking and Wi-Fi?
faq.a: Yes to both — there's free on-site parking and free Wi-Fi. As a small stay, parking is easy without circling for a space, which suits self-drivers. Every room also has Netflix and a private balcony.

faq.q: What's the noise like at IKKYU2?
faq.a: Some reviews note that you hear the odd footstep along the corridor, as it's a small building. If you're a light sleeper, bring earplugs or ask for a room off the main corridor when you book.

It's a strong choice for anyone wanting a clean, quiet, private room in central Ang Thong at a low price, and for travellers who like small boutique stays. It suits a restful stay or a stop on a longer trip, as long as you're fine without breakfast and can live with a little corridor noise.
